watch.text: First-choice striker Igor Thiago is suspended for three Premier League games, starting vs Everton on Nov 23.
Defenders Nathan Collins and Aaron Hickey (hurt on international duty) are out for several weeks; Rico Henry and Kaye Furo also out.
Fabio Carvalho has a strong chance to be in the squad after missing the last four games, per Keith Andrews.
Everton report no injury concerns after the international break; Jack Grealish, out after an illness and a club-protocol breach, is confirmed available by David Moyes.
Striker João Pedro (thigh) is out until about January, confirmed by Xabi Alonso before the Leeds game; Reece James (knee surgery) is also out until about January.
Moisés Caicedo went off after 21 minutes of the 4-1 loss to Leeds on Nov 21 with a back knock; no return date, Alonso hopes to have him for Forest on Nov 27.
Neco Williams (arm, hurt vs Ipswich) started the 2-0 loss at Bournemouth on Nov 22 despite being a doubt; Nicolás Domínguez is out until about January.
Mauricio Pochettino took charge for the Nov 22 game at Liverpool: a new manager, so past results are a weaker guide.
Striker Benjamin Šeško (shin) has been out since late October with no return date; Marcus Rashford (hip), Luke Shaw, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are also out.
Jean-Philippe Mateta and Yéremy Pino are reported suspended for the Hull game on Nov 29, and Ismaïla Sarr (groin) is out (OG.com preview citing the Premier League list).
Midfielder Tim Iroegbunam went off in the first half vs Brighton with a hamstring problem and awaits an MRI, per Hull's manager.
Spurs are without Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert (knees), Mathys Tel and Mykhailo Mudryk; Sandro Tonali (illness) and Tosin Adarabioyo are doubts for Sunderland on Nov 29.
Joint-top scorer Brian Brobbey (thigh) and Granit Xhaka (calf, longer) missed the Villa game and have no return date; Dan Ballard and Romaine Mundle are out until late December.
Antoine Semenyo (knee) is out; City drew 1-1 with Fulham on Nov 21, now four league games without a win.
Anton Stach, Noah Okafor and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are all back in full training and Daniel Farke reports no injuries; Leeds then beat Chelsea 4-1 on Nov 21.
Goalkeeper David Raya hurt his shoulder in the 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Nov 21; MRI ordered, Arteta called it 'not good news', later reports say no surgery needed.
Bukayo Saka is about four weeks from a return (eight-week injury, per Arteta) and Martín Zubimendi (hamstring, hurt with Spain) is out for a few weeks.
William Saliba was available for the first time this season after a long-term back problem.

401879225.summary: Our xG model makes Forest the favorite while the market backs Chelsea; Chelsea's absences (João Pedro, Reece James, a Caicedo knock) point our way, so nothing found justifies the market's price.

reasons.text: Chelsea are without striker João Pedro and Reece James until about January, and Caicedo went off with a back knock in the 4-1 loss to Leeds.
Forest lost 2-0 at Bournemouth on Nov 22; Neco Williams (arm) played through a doubt.

401879226.summary: Brentford are without suspended striker Igor Thiago (three games) and defenders Collins and Hickey, which covers most of why the market is higher on United than our xG model.

reasons.text: Igor Thiago, Brentford's first-choice striker, is suspended for three league games starting Nov 23 (this is the second).
Brentford defenders Nathan Collins and Aaron Hickey are out for several weeks; Rico Henry is also out.
Against it: United have a new manager (Pochettino, from Nov 22) and are without Šeško, Rashford, Shaw, Baleba and Ugarte.

401878750.summary: Thiago's suspension (third game) and Brentford's missing defenders explain part of the market's lean to Arsenal, but Arsenal are also missing Saka, Zubimendi and possibly Raya.

reasons.text: Brentford striker Igor Thiago serves the last game of a three-match ban here; Collins and Hickey are out for several weeks.
Arsenal: Saka about four weeks away, Zubimendi out a few weeks, Raya's shoulder under assessment; Saliba is back.

returning.text: Available for the first time this season after a back problem.

401879230.summary: The market backs Palace much more than our model even though Palace are reported to be without suspended Mateta and Pino and injured Sarr; Hull's Iroegbunam hamstring is the only point the market's way.

reasons.text: Mateta and Pino reported suspended for this game, Sarr (groin) out (OG.com preview).
Hull midfielder Tim Iroegbunam (hamstring) awaits an MRI after going off vs Brighton.

401879224.summary: Sunderland are missing joint-top scorer Brobbey, Xhaka and two more starters, which explains part of the market's lean to Spurs, but Spurs have a long injury list of their own.

reasons.text: Sunderland: Brobbey (thigh) and Xhaka (calf) out with no return date; Ballard and Mundle out until late December.
Spurs: Xavi Simons, Odobert, Tel and Mudryk out; Tonali (illness) and Adarabioyo doubtful.

401879220.summary: Nothing found that justifies the market's lean to Forest at Hull beyond Hull's Iroegbunam hamstring scare; Forest lost 2-0 at Bournemouth on Nov 22.

reasons.text: Hull midfielder Tim Iroegbunam (hamstring) awaits an MRI.

401879218.summary: The market backs City far more than our model despite City's four-game league winless run and Semenyo's absence, while Leeds have a fully fit squad after a 4-1 win at Chelsea.

reasons.text: City drew 1-1 with Fulham on Nov 21, four league games without a win; Semenyo (knee) out.
Leeds report no injuries, with Stach, Okafor and Calvert-Lewin back in full training.
